Preparing CSV and Excel data

Source: vignettes/input-data-formats.Rmd
input-data-formats.Rmd

metapropul expects one row per independent study or comparison. CSV and Excel headers can use any names: function arguments and the graphical interface map your headers to their statistical roles. Numeric analysis columns must contain numbers rather than formatted strings such as "12%" or "1,250".

The optional study column identifies studies and the optional subgroup column identifies a completely observed subgroup. Merely having a subgroup column in the file does not request subgroup analysis: subgroup = NULL is the function default, and the GUI always starts at None. Select a subgroup only when it is scientifically intended. Avoid duplicate study labels where possible. The GUI shows the required headers for the selected analysis and provides a downloadable CSV template.

Ratio outcomes: OR, RR, and HR

Odds ratios and risk ratios can be calculated from a 2 by 2 table:

study event_e n_e event_c n_c subgroup
Study 1 12 100 20 100 Europe
Study 2 8 80 15 75 Asia 
meta_ratio(dat, "event_e", "n_e", "event_c", "n_c",
  studylab = "study", subgroup = "subgroup", measure = "OR")

Reported OR, RR, or HR values can be supplied with confidence limits. These three columns are on the ordinary ratio scale and must be positive:

study effect lower upper
Study 1 0.72 0.51 1.02
Study 2 1.18 0.88 1.58 
meta_ratio(dat, effect = "effect", lower = "lower", upper = "upper",
  studylab = "study", measure = "HR")

Log OR, log RR, or log HR may instead be supplied with its standard error:

study log_effect se
Study 1 -0.329 0.177
Study 2 0.165 0.150 
meta_ratio(dat, effect = "log_effect", se = "se", effect_scale = "log",
  studylab = "study", measure = "HR")

Hazard ratios cannot be reconstructed from simple event totals; use one of the two pre-computed formats. Do not enter a ratio as effect when effect_scale = "log".

Continuous outcomes

Raw MD or SMD analysis requires both group summaries:

study mean_e sd_e n_e mean_c sd_c n_c
Study 1 12.1 3.2 60 14.0 3.5 58
Study 2 10.8 2.9 45 12.2 3.1 47

Alternatively, use effect, lower, and upper for a reported MD or SMD. Use meta_generic() for a continuous effect supplied with an SE or variance.

Proportions

Provide event counts and total sample sizes. Each event count must lie between zero and its corresponding total:

study event n subgroup
Study 1 18 200 Hospital
Study 2 7 95 Community

Generic inverse-variance effects

Provide effect plus exactly one of se, variance, or the pair lower and upper. Effects stay on their analysis scale. For a log ratio and SE, choose backtransform = "exp"; for an untransformed estimate choose "identity".

Correlations and incidence rates

Correlation analysis requires cor and n; correlations must be strictly between -1 and 1 and n must exceed 3. Incidence-rate analysis requires non-negative event and positive person_time columns.

Risk-of-bias files

Use one row per study, one study-label column, and one column per ROB domain. Labels must match the fitted meta-analysis exactly when creating a combined forest and ROB figure. Judgements must use the levels of the selected tool, for example Low, Some concerns, and High for a generic three-level tool.

Meta-regression prediction files

Fit meta-regression using moderator columns in the primary study dataset. A prediction file contains only the moderator combinations to estimate: its headers and data types must match the moderators used in the model. Do not add effect estimates or standard errors. The GUI creates a template from the fitted model so categorical levels and numeric columns are preserved.

Umbrella-review results

Use one row per reported meta-analysis result. Required columns are outcome, review, effect, lower, and upper. Useful optional columns include measure, studies, participants, i2, p_value, year, quality, and certainty. Each row remains a separate reported synthesis; metapropul does not pool rows across reviews.

Primary-study overlap (CCA)

CCA input is long-format membership data:

review primary_study outcome included
Review A Study 1 Mortality TRUE
Review A Study 2 Mortality TRUE
Review B Study 1 Mortality TRUE

review and primary_study are required. outcome and included are optional. An inclusion indicator may contain only TRUE/FALSE, 1/0, or NA; NA means that the review–study cell is structurally unavailable.

Primary-study diagnostics within reviews

Use one row per primary-study estimate with outcome, review, primary_study, effect, lower, and upper; participant count is optional. Every outcome–review group needs at least two unique primary studies. These data are diagnosed within each source review and are never pooled across reviews.
